title: CHILD
idiom: Ardizzone-like ink and watercolour wash, a child on the doorstep of a great house
hero_prompt: Ink and watercolour illustration in the manner of Edward Ardizzone, a loose pen line with pale flat washes, hand-made on paper, flat and graphic with visible pen line and watercolour paper texture, not a photograph, not a 3D render, no depth-of-field, wide panoramic composition: a small boy of about six, seen from behind, kneeling on the stone doorstep of an enormous old house and stacking plain wooden building blocks into a wobbly tower beside him on the step; the great front door behind him stands open a hand's width with warm light falling out across the step, and tall windows of the house rise up and away above him, a few of them lit. The child is tiny against the house; generous empty pale space at the sides. Washes of ochre, sage green and soft brick red on cream.
icon_prompt: Linocut emblem, a flat single-colour black silhouette on an ochre ground, no shading or gradients: a very small child standing in front of a tall arched doorway, holding up one square building block in a raised hand, the doorway more than three times the child's height. Bold, high-contrast, no fine linework, reads clearly at 24 pixels.
